content: Accelerate clinical trials across patients, sponsors, sites, and more on a flexible and compliant platform. Clinical engagement helps clinical research organizations raise trial awareness with candidates, speed up onboarding, and mitigate attrition. Empower candidates to discover trials, evaluate eligibility, and sign up for eligible trials with self-service portals. Streamline participant enrollment with optimized auto-matching and consent management features.

Before setting up specific clinical engagement features, perform foundational tasks: (1) Enable person accounts — all patients/members must be modeled as person accounts. (2) Install OmniStudio for guided interactions and rich user experiences without code. (3) Set up healthcare providers — practitioners (doctors, nurses, therapists) and facilities (hospitals, clinics, labs). (4) Create profiles and assign permission sets. (5) Verify data protection details are available in records. (6) Use Data Loader for bulk import of code data (diagnosis codes, procedure codes). After loading, restrict user access to code objects to Read-Only to prevent unauthorized modifications that could interfere with automated approval processes.
gotchas: Data integrity in code database is critical — restrict code objects to Read-Only after initial load
Code changes by users can interfere with automated approval processes
OmniStudio is web-only — not available on mobile/iPad app

content: Manage clinical trial sites — the physical locations where trials are conducted. Site management includes: site setup and configuration, site-participant associations, site coordinator roles, device registration per site, and multi-site trial coordination. Agentic AI capabilities are available for site management automation, including prebuilt flows and agent topics for streamlining site-related workflows.
gotchas: Site management has separate agentic AI capabilities requiring additional licenses
Site coordinators use Experience Cloud — separate from the clinical trial manager web interface

description: Adverse Event (AE) objects capture safety reports during clinical interactions. AE records link to the contact/patient who experienced the event, the product involved, and the healthcare provider who reported it. AE severity classification (Mild, Moderate, Severe, Life-Threatening, Fatal) drives regulatory reporting timelines. Serious AE auto-escalation rules trigger compliance workflows. Integration with safety databases (e.g., ARGUS) requires outbound event-driven patterns.
setup_steps: Configure AE record types aligned to regulatory classification
Configure outbound integration to safety databases
Set up reporting timeline validation rules
gotchas: Regulatory reporting timelines vary by severity and jurisdiction
AE records must capture the reporter, patient, product, AND event - all four are required for a valid report
Integration with safety databases must be event-driven, not batch, for serious AEs
migration_relevance: Veeva AE reporting maps to Adverse Event objects. Safety database integration patterns differ.

description: Site Management supports clinical trial site identification, selection, and management. Criteria-based search allows filtering sites by geography, therapeutic area, patient population, investigator experience, and performance metrics. Site records link to accounts (healthcare facilities), contacts (investigators), and clinical trials. Site feasibility assessments capture structured evaluation data.
setup_steps: Configure site record types and evaluation criteria
Configure geolocation data for proximity search
gotchas: Geolocation fields must be populated for proximity-based site search
Site-investigator relationships are many-to-many via junction objects
Feasibility assessment criteria should be configurable per therapeutic area
migration_relevance: Net-new capability for most migrations. May overlap with custom CTMS implementations.
